test_title: PYST 81: SSC CGL 2024 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On 26 Sept, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: A shopkeeper has a fault of 100 g in a 3 kg weight. He sold 3 kg of potatoes to Charu using the same faulty weight for ₹46. The cost price of the potatoes for the seller was ₹12 per kg. How much profit (in ₹) did he earn on the potatoes?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Actual weight given by shopkeeper = 3 kg − 0.1 kg = 2.9 kg

Actual CP for 2.9 kg = 2.9 × 12 = ₹34.8

Profit = Selling Price (SP) − Actual CP = 46 − 34.8 = ₹11.2

**∴ The correct answer is ₹11.2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Claimed weight = 3 kg = 3000 g

⇒ Fault in weight = 100 g

⇒ Cost Price (CP) of potatoes = ₹12 per kg

⇒ Selling Price (SP) charged to Charu = ₹46

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/604ab613ad25927132e16961b8a2e7f72d7c781a616ceea8b49b5a7c889c6443.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Actual weight of potatoes given to Charu = 3000 g − 100 g

⇒ Actual weight = 2900 g = 2.9 kg

⇒ Actual Cost Price (CP) incurred by the shopkeeper = Actual weight × CP per kg

⇒ Actual CP = 2.9 × 12 = ₹34.8

⇒ Profit earned = Selling Price (SP) − Actual Cost Price (CP)

⇒ Profit = 46 − 34.8 = ₹11.2

**∴ The correct answer is ₹11.2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer (Weight Fault)

When a shopkeeper uses a false weight to cheat customers, the absolute actual cost price (CP) is calculated strictly on the true amount of goods given, while the selling price (SP) is obtained from the customer based on the false claimed weight.

Basic Profit & Loss Formula

Profit occurs when Selling Price (SP) is greater than the Cost Price (CP). The fundamental equation is Profit = SP − CP. If percentage is asked, Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100%.

Marked Price & Discount

Sellers often mark up their goods above the original CP and then provide a discount. The Selling Price is derived as SP = Marked Price (MP) − Discount. The final realized profit remains SP − Actual CP.
